title: Room to discover who you can become.
intro: Understand powerful AI, ask better questions and create something of your own. This proposal connects young people’s agency with ethical technology, trusted adults and real opportunities to grow.

title: A future with more possibilities.
intro: The proposal connects everyday childhood opportunity with a wider question: how can young people share in the capabilities of increasingly powerful intelligence?

title: Start with your own interests.
intro: A supported computing station offers a place to make, learn and reflect. The young person brings the meaning; the record can change as their understanding grows.

title: Understand the rules around you.
intro: Follow a question to a readable source. Learn why a rule exists, whose decision it affects and what needs checking in the present setting.

title: Make something. Find your next step.
intro: A small creative project can reveal what someone enjoys, what gets in the way and which person or resource would help them continue.

title: Keep the relationships that matter.
intro: A life can hold several important relationships. Chosen memories, useful information and cultural connections need room to retain their meaning through change.

title: A wider view of adult life.
intro: Mentors, practical work experience, shared productive ownership and planned time for life offer different possibilities to investigate as young people grow into adulthood.

title: Belong through shared everyday life.
intro: A useful task, a shared meal or a welcoming invitation can connect people. Communities choose their recognition, while essential support remains independent of contribution.

title: A local beginning. A long horizon.
intro: Local learning and a lasting volunteer network connect the Olympic horizon with young adults investigating the future of their communities, Earth and space.

title: Real people. Clear choices.
intro: The young person can ask questions, correct a record and turn to accountable adults. Learning, recording, research and publication each need an understandable purpose and actual arrangements.

title: Begin where people can follow through.
intro: A useful pilot needs a willing host, time, support and something concrete to try. Young people help shape it, and what happens changes the next step.

title: Follow the proposal to its sources.
intro: Read the unchanged original, follow every project and public-guidance reference, and distinguish the proposal from evidence about outcomes.

title: Find the part you want to explore.
intro: Related projects offer background, tools and development directions. Each has its own scope and status; a link does not establish a service or partnership.

title: Authorship, rights and this website.
intro: A public reading guide to Luke Nathan Hayes’s proposal, with the original document, exact source links and clearly identified concept artwork.

title: Choose your own route.
intro: Follow the chapters in sequence or begin with the question that matters to you.
